summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a complex history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, hypogammaglobulinemia, prior stem cell transplant, and recurrent diverticulosis was admitted for worsening left lower quadrant abdominal pain and diarrhea. CT imaging confirmed acute sigmoid diverticulitis without perforation or abscess. She was treated with IV fluids, IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone and metronidazole), and transitioned to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. Oral vancomycin was continued as C. difficile prophylaxis. Her pain improved, she advanced to a regular diet, and was ambulating independently. A right leg ultrasound ruled out DVT. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics, vancomycin, and her baseline medications with follow-up plans for her pancreatic cyst, eye condition, and chronic pain.
problems: Diverticulitis of large intestine without perforation or abscess without bleeding
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
